transcript.text: Dropped a cast iron pan on my ceramic hob and there's a crack right across the front left ring. It still heats up. Can I keep using it until I get a new one?

No, stop using it and switch the hob off at its wall isolator or the fuse box until the glass is replaced. Even though it still heats, a crack across a ring can let spills or cleaning water reach live parts underneath, which is a shock risk, and heat can make the crack spread or the glass break. That fits that zone's element or its control. Once that is sorted, run it again: does it work normally now?
Ok, I'll stop using it. Some pasta water spilled earlier and might have got into the crack. There's a red cooker switch on the wall, so I can turn it off there. What do I do about getting it fixed?

Water near the plug or socket is dangerous. Please don't touch the plug, socket or machine if they or your hands are wet. If you can do it safely, switch off the circuit at the consumer unit (fuse box), keep away from the water, and don't use the machine again until a qualified electrician or appliance engineer has checked it. That fits that zone's element or its control.

Ok, I'll switch it off at the red cooker switch. It's a hob not a machine by the way. Who should I call to get it checked and replaced, an electrician or Hotpoint? I can't get to the model label as the oven is underneath.

Call Hotpoint's own service team or an appliance repair engineer, because replacing a cracked glass top is an appliance repair; an electrician is only needed if the cooker supply or wall switch itself is faulty. Hotpoint will likely ask for the model or serial number, so look for it on the manual, receipt or registration paperwork since the label can't be reached. That fits that zone's element or its control.
